questions.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm
questions.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{5}⁡(5x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5} \\ {v}^{′}=25{x}^{4}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 25{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x=5{x}^{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 25{x}^{4}{log}_{5}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{5}⁡(5x)\cdot (5{x}^{5})-\int \frac{5{x}^{5}}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{x}^{5}{log}_{5}⁡(5x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\int 5{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{x}^{5}{log}_{5}⁡(5x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\cdot {x}^{5}+C \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(5\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x)-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{5}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}.$

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{4}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{4}⁡(2x)}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{4}⁡(2x)\cdot (-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}})-\int (-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{4}⁡(2x)}{3{x}^{3}}+\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{4}⁡(2x)}{3{x}^{3}}+\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡4}(-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}})+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-\frac{1}{9{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C \\  & =-\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1}{9{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{4}⁡(2x)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}.$

questions.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{8}{{x}^{5}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{8}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{8\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})-\int (-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{4}}+2\int \frac{1}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{1}{2{x}^{4}}+C \\  & =-\frac{4\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{2{x}^{4}}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

questions.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
questions.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/3}^{e}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1/3}^{e}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1/3}^{e}-{\int }_{1/3}^{e}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x){|}_{1/3}^{e}-{\int }_{1/3}^{e}x(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡(3e)-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡1-{\int }_{1/3}^{e}\,\text{d}x \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡(3e)-x{|}_{1/3}^{e}\, \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡(3e)-(e-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡3+e-e+\frac{1}{3} \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡3+\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{0}^{({e}^{2}-1)/4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x+1)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{0}^{({e}^{2}-1)/4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x+1)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x+1)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{4}{4x+1} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int 1\cdot \,dx=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{({e}^{2}-1)/4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x+1)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{({e}^{2}-1)/4}u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{0}^{({e}^{2}-1)/4}-{\int }_{0}^{({e}^{2}-1)/4}v{u}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x+1)\,(x){|}_{0}^{({e}^{2}-1)/4}-{\int }_{0}^{({e}^{2}-1)/4}x(\frac{4}{4x+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})(\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{4})-{\int }_{0}^{({e}^{2}-1)/4}\frac{4x}{4x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{4}\cdot 2-{\int }_{0}^{({e}^{2}-1)/4}(1-\frac{1}{4x+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2}-{[x-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x+1)]}_{0}^{({e}^{2}-1)/4} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2}-(\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{4}-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2}-(\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{4}-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}({e}^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$
